commit.message:
CLI: no capture command; an agent takes the picture with its own tools (#83)

## What and why

OpenFilm's core keeps only what an agent can't do on its own. Taking a
picture of a live web page is something any agent can do with its own
tools: a browser tool it has, or a few lines of Playwright (`npx
playwright screenshot <url> <file.png>`). So `openfilm capture` goes:

- `packages/openfilm/src/capture.mjs` and its test are removed.
- The CLI drops the command, its help, and its options (`--size`,
`--full`, `--wait`, `--dark`, `--click`, `--hide`, `--selector`).
`--scale` stays; `render` uses it.
- The three READMEs drop its line.
- The keynote and screen-demo skills no longer point to it. They still
require the real product, and the agent captures it with its own tools.
The copy is synced from openfilm/skills `1111136` (`pnpm skills:sync`).

Nothing else used `capture.mjs`: Studio and the desktop app don't depend
on it.

## Testing

- `pnpm typecheck` passes.
- `pnpm skills:sync --check`: the copy is openfilm/skills at `1111136`.
`pnpm audit:public`: no findings.
- `openfilm --help` no longer lists `capture`; `openfilm capture …`
exits 2 with "no command capture".
- The full test suite runs on CI.

A `patch` changeset is included.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
